text.title: RSpec Testing for Rails Applications Output Contract
text.summary: Pins the shape of a valid RSpec Testing for Rails Applications output. Subagent MUST satisfy this contract before returning to caller.

required.field: the actual answer / chosen option / value produced
at least 2 sentences; cites at least one input artefact by name
list of input names with source paths or URLs

forbidden.pattern: rationale that does not reference any input by name
inputs_used empty AND decision is not 'no-op'
duplicate artefact_id within the same store

allowed-transformations.transformation: Trim rationale to no more than 500 chars, preserving numeric claims and named tools.
Promote 'no decision yet' to status='pending' rather than fabricating a decision.
Group near-duplicate inputs, recording the group with member count.

section.title: Spec-file contract (what the artefact describes)
section.p: The artefact above records the DECISION. This section pins the shape of each spec file that decision produces — the machine-checkable half.

example.note: Wrong filename convention; no describe/context/it; `create` everywhere; not isolated; no shared examples; unused `let!`; 600 lines.

list.item: `it "does X" do ... end` at top level with no enclosing `describe`.
`create(:order)` in a spec that never asserts on persisted state.
A service spec that requires `rails_helper` despite testing pure Ruby logic.
Every required field populated with a typed value
No forbidden pattern matches the output
Every spec file follows describe / context / it and stays under 300 lines
Unit specs use build_stubbed and require spec_helper, not rails_helper
Cross-class invariants live in shared_examples_for, not per-class copies
